text_fidelity_a:
B. Toys by Battat B’S Eye View Peg Puzzle Dexterity Toy – Classic Wooden Puzzles for Toddlers with 9 Chunkypiece – Natural Wood Toddler Puzzles, Model:BX1264Z Toddlers love to play and they benefit from toys that encourage learning or help in other areas of development. One toy that seems promising in these ways is the B’S Eye View Peg Puzzle Dexterity Toy – Classic Wooden Puzzle for Toddlers.

This puzzle has knobs on the pieces, making it easy for toddlers to grab each piece. It helps with coordination, too, as little ones will learn to fit the right shape into the right slot. However, the colors of the pieces are washed out and they really need to be an eye catching primary. Not only would it be more inviting to toddlers and preschoolers but it would provide an opportunity to not only teach numbers and counting, but color recognition too while playing.

Another issue with the pieces is that the details are lacking. If you are going to add detail make it something a child can recognize. But probably the most shocking oversight is the shapes and numbers that they are supposed to match. There is an octagon, for example, that represents the number 7, a five- pointed star that is used for the number 8, and so on. Why would you do this? The octagon should be the number 8 and the star should match with number 5. This is an oversight that someone should have caught.

Other issues I have are with the puzzle holes- they are a little too big and this would be hard to travel anywhere with. I do like that the numbers are nice and big and easy to see and that the knobs are big and tall enough for tiny fingers to grasp. While I haven’t seen it happen yet I do worry because, since they are very much like thumbtacks, they may come loose and eventually get lost. The pieces don’t hold in place as well as I would like.

Toddler toys that help kids learn are nice and while the B’S Eye View Peg Puzzle Dexterity Toy – Classic Wooden Puzzle for Toddlers does help with coordination and other skills, it lacks in other areas. The oversight with the numbers and shapes not matching is a big one and I have other issues, too. So, when I think of everything as a whole, this toy gets a thumbs down from me.
text_fidelity_b: B. Toys by Battat B’S Eye View Peg Puzzle Dexterity Toy – Classic Wooden Puzzles for Toddlers with 9 Chunkypiece – Natural Wood Toddler Puzzles, Model:BX1264Z

text_fidelity_a:
CATAN 3D EDITION Board Strategy Game with Immersive 3D Tiles | Adventure Game | Family Game for Adults and Kids | Ages 12+ | 3-4 Players | Average Playtime 60-90 Minutes I started playing Settlers of Catan when it first came out, many years ago. It has a special place as a gateway game. It brought people who wouldn't normally play anything exotic out of the world of Chutes and Ladders, and into the realm of strategy board games. It's easier to learn than Monopoly, but without the very lengthy period of regret between knowing who will win and actually reaching the foregone conclusion. I largely stopped playing the game about 20 years ago because thanks to Catan, the world of board games exploded into a great variety of games that I consider to be much better. Seeing this fancy set made me want to give it a try again, see what might have changed, and teach the kids.

Unboxing:
The components are visible in the packaging, which is unusual. The outer box is a throwaway, but there is a good sturdy box inside. Everything is packed well enough to avoid shifting and scuffing in transit. There are a few too many components for my taste. It takes quite a while to get everything taken out and put away. I'm fine with that if a game really needs that level of complexity, but I think this one is pushing it. The new three dimensional components make it even more of a chore. I like that the water border clips together securely. In the original, the water spaces tended to slide around, and since the game is about building roads and houses on the cracks, it was destabilizing for everything. Now the board stays together securely, even on carpet.

The new three dimensional tiles are a fun idea, but poorly implemented. Each one needs a convex, translucent, slippery disc on top, but few allowances were made for this in design. They just teeter there and slip around, or sit way off center. I can't support making the number circles translucent. I can't see any positive purpose for it, and it reduces the ability to play with variants that start with some of them face down. After assembling the sea sections, I see that the game board is smaller than I expected. I really like the addition of harbor shapes on the seas to show where the ports should go. The ports themselves are a bit hard to see compared to the old cardboard ones.

The colors chosen for each player are questionable. The parts themselves have a dark wash over them to make the details stand out, but it makes them all dingy. Beige, orange, red, and blue. I guess the blue player can find their pieces, but in dim lighting, the rest look too similar. There's an odd mix of unique things, like the shape of each player's houses, and having things repeat that could have been unique, like all of the forest hexes being identical.

If the instruction book is hard to open, it's because it isn't a book, it's a foldout that folds counterintuitively. There is a quick reference startup guide and another small book with more in-depth details.

It's nice that it comes with card holders, and while it's a chore to get everything back in the box right, at least there's a secure place for everything. The gameplay is as I remember. Simple and engaging enough for most people to be willing to play, and strategic enough to be satisfying. There are games that are both simpler and more strategic out there. Quite a lot of them. In a four player game, anyone who ends up hemmed in by players who chose after them can end up stuck without anywhere to expand. This leads to occasional games like Monopoly, where someone isn't going to be having much fun for an hour. Luck can play a bit too heavily. This was one of the early games that added the excellent mechanic of randomizing the playing field, but the dice too often just end up rolling the same number over and over, which tends to give some players a lot to do and others nothing for several critical turns.

It's strange, but I think I may actually stick with my old plain set. This one feels more fancy and less functional.
text_fidelity_b: CATAN 3D EDITION Board Strategy Game with Immersive 3D Tiles | Adventure Game | Family Game for Adults and Kids | Ages 12+ | 3-4 Players | Average Playtime 60-90 Minutes

Terra by Battat – Wild Life Set – Realistic Animal Toy Figures with Elephant Toys for Kids 3+ (6 Pc) I have mixed feelings about this animal hospital. Overall, the structure itself is extremely sturdy and there are a lot of wonderful ideas in the construction. The roof swings up and down with a hinge, and while it's heavy enough that I have some cringes about someone getting a finger stuck, overall that concern has not panned out. The overall structure is very sturdy, but then the little animal pens have extremely flimsy doors, one of which didn't work right out the gate, and refuses to close. A second door also occasionally refuses to close, which makes me think that this is a design issue rather than a actual broken product. The really cool little deck that has a string fence is really a neat idea, but then it was implemented in such a flimsy fashion that it is really not that fun to play with because it keeps coming apart.

Overall I want to like this more, but when I compare it to something by Schleich which just has all of the details really dialed in to where nothing breaks or comes apart all the time, it's clear that there is a difference in quality. This is made nicely in some ways, but then falls short on some of those finished details.

I will also note that it took me a lot longer to assemble than I wish. I really think that they should have assembled some more parts of it and shipped it as a partly assembled things so that I didn't have to spend so much time putting it together. I have small children I would rather be hanging out with.

text_fidelity_a:
UGears Models 3-D Wooden Puzzle - Mechanical Horse Mechanoid This horse is striking in appearance. It looks wild and spirited. It is quite a conversation piece on its looks alone. I would give it five stars alone for that. Movement is not as spectacular, but it does move. There’s a winding key and start/stop control levers. The horse is not able to take more than 5 steps without halting or simply falling over. It looks like the last motions of a horse before succumbing to the effects of a trank dart. The kit is a real bear to assemble. The instructions must be heeded. You may find you have to flip ahead a few pages at times to see just what this subassembly is that you are working on and where it is supposed to go. I knew at the start that I would need to sand the pieces and use the provided wax. Ther's not a whole lot of wax. It’s a 1 inch slice of a candle but the important thing is that it enough for the horse. The wax is somewhat soft, like beeswax. I had no problem with missing pieces. There are six boards with laser cut parts. If you don't see anything missing, you have all the parts. Assembly is a bit tedious and somewhat painful. As the model continues to take shape and become more horse-like there is the adrenalin surge all model builders feel when they are nearing the end. Once assembly is completed the key is wound and switch is moved. My model just sat there. C’mon little horsy, let’s go. Well, back-winding the key overcomes the initial friction and horse begins to haltingly show movement. Lots of going back and forth with the key helps to distribute the wax and the horse becomes more limber. After lots of massaging like this you can get the horse to take 4 or maybe 5 steps. Max is 9 and only rarely achieved. It will usually fall over to announce it is finished walking. Well and good. It is still a cool model and I would build one again. I’m giving it 5 stars but 4 would be reasonable too. I wish it walked a bit better and that the instructions had a bit of expository text. This is a worthwhile model that will occupy 8 hours of your life in assembly. It is ingenious.

I have a few hints on this horse:
Mine locked up once while fully wound up. I could not get it to operate at all. I tried moving the legs and rapping the body with my knuckles. Nothing! My horse was dead. It was not until I grasped the horses neck and moved it forward and back that the gears unlocked. This only happened once, but it was super frustrating as I was contemplating opening up the entire model to fix it.

Understand at the outset that this horse can’t walk for long. If you watch the clever videos the horse appears to leave its stall and seems to be on a journey to a pasture or whatever. If you look closely the horse only takes a few steps in each scene. Clever editing makes it look like the horse can go on a pastoral journey. Not really complaining because all the ad copy and literature says the horse can’t go far. This is only a problem if your expectations are too high and unrealistic. It is what it is, a model of mechanical horse. So enjoy that as I do I.

My rubber band broke. I suppose it had a nick in it that grew over time. I was able to cut out the broken piece and retie the rubber band but it is not easy working in the body of the assembled model. So do examine the length of the rubber band before assembly.

Update on the rubber band issue 5 days later:
The rubber band broke again. No, I haven’t over wound it. I’ll have to see if I can get a replacement from somewhere.

The rubber bands for the horse’s mane and tail are genius. Looks great and the bands lie perfectly when cut. I was worried I’d need hair styling skills to make the horse look good. It was no problem.

Seriously, sand everything. Knock down the edges of the large pieces as well so they lose their painful sharpness. If you have to reach into the interior of the model later you will be glad you did.

Some parts are seeming impossible to press together with human hands. I finally resorted to a small furniture clamp with soft jaws to supplement my finger strength. I think pliers or small c-clamp would work, as well.

A cushiony work surface was helpful in supporting a board while I was breaking a part loose from the board. I used towel I use for assembly projects.

It really takes 8 uninterrupted hours to assemble this model no matter how skilled you think you are. If you leave out trying to be extra careful and the extra sanding I guess you could do it in about five.

On page 13 of the instructions I was confused. The diagram seems to suggest that the rubber band should be folded upon itself in thirds. After puzzling on this I covinced myself that doubling the band was correct and it turned out to be right choice.

Check for proper operation of parts during assembly. In some steps you are "told" to operate the key and check that the parts move freely. This is very important. Once the horse is fully assembled getting back inside it is a difficult task since gear timing must be maintained.

There is a down side to using the wax. Your hands will get a coating of wax and when that is transferred to the horse there will be discolored spots. Try to keep the wax from where you don't want the wood to darken. I washed my hands frequently and still ended up with a horse that is more pinto than wood white.

There are no troubleshooting hints in the instructions. If you can't find help on the website you are on your own. I do have a vibe from Ugears that they are helpful and I think you can correspond with them and get help if you have a bad problem.
text_fidelity_b: UGears Models 3-D Wooden Puzzle - Mechanical Horse Mechanoid

Schleich Dinosaurs, Realistic Large Dinosaur Toys for Boys and Girls, Barapasaurus Toy Figurine, Ages 4+ As usual with Schleich toys, you can’t fault the durability or the quality. I’ve reviewed a number of them, and I can’t speak highly enough of their quality builds. They are made to last, even if roughly played with. We’ve had several now for about a decade, and they look no different than when they arrived, despite having gone through a number of dino “battles” and the like. This one is no exception. One issue I suppose is that it may be a little over-built in that it has quite a heft to it, which may preclude younger children from playing easily with it. It’s sizable already, but add the weight and I can see small hands having a difficult time picking it up and moving it around, or certainly moving it smoothly. Once you move past the toddler years, though, that will be much less of an issue.

In terms of looks, it’s nicely painted (again, as usual with Schleich), with the blue cuts running down central area from head to tail tip standing out particularly nicely. The pose is as if it is about to take a step forward or perhaps step on something (someone?). The face is my one real complaint about this model. It’s a raw sort of red color, which isn’t all that aesthetic. It almost looks like it’s been flayed, or perhaps is furiously angry. And there’s something about the mouth being open in the manner it is that just seems a bit off-putting.But at least the teeth look like the right sort (I hate when one has, for instance, obviously carnivorous teeth on herbivores).

It’s nice to have a new model and a relatively unknown one at that. Outside of the head/face, which is a relatively minor complaint, the barapasuaruk is another fine addition to a great line of toys/models.

text_fidelity_a: Hot Wheels id Smart Track Starter Kit with 3 Exclusive Cars, Track Pieces and Hot Wheels Race Portal for Physical & Digital Play, Gift for Kids Ages 8 Years Old & Up This is okay. If not for Vine, I'm not sure I would spend this type of money though. The one good thing is that there is some hand/eye coordination in play, so your children well get some development. You see they have to view an app, which shows a speedometer. They need to keep the needle at a certain speed. Speedometer graphics is broken down into 2 colors, blue and red. If you go to the red, chances are good your car will fly off the tracks. How do you control the speed? By pumping the booster. The faster you pump, the needle will move towards the red. So you need to time yourself and not pump too slow, or too fast to keep the needle in the blue at all times. My kids seem to think it's fun, so that's all that matters. Science Kit for Kids Crystal Growing Kit + Light Up Display Dome for Kids by Creative Kids, Make Your Own Grow 4 Large Crystals, DIY Educational Experiment - Cool STEM Gift for Boys & Girls Lengthy process and involved more parental involvement than anticipated but it was worth it and kiddo loves his new room decor. We did have to clear out a small cupboard for a little over a week to keep the growing crystals away from our cats. They couldn't be trusted to leave it be.

Tips:
1. Stir stir stir. The more complete you get the powders to dissolve the better the crystals come out.
2. If the crystals start to peek outside the top of the water, pull that one out and let it dry (Ours didn't all grow at the same rate). They come out smoother if they don't keep growing out of the water.
3. Once formed the crystals are delicate and brittle so this really is a place and leave alone type thing.
4. We let ours grow for a little bit over a week, so they got pretty sizable. I would suggest leaving them in there until they start to peel above the water, then pull them out.

Jurassic World Bite 'n Fight Tyrannosaurus Rex in Larger Size with Realistic Sculpting, Articulation and Dual-Button Activation for Tail Strike and Head Strikes, Ages 4 and Older Wow! Wow wow wow!

That's pretty much what you're going to hear when you present this gift to a small person. A bunch of wows, and then a bunch of roaring after you get it out of the package and they start playing with it. There are two buttons in the middle of the T Rex, one of which works the tail and the other of which works the head and snapping jaws. The buttons are a little hard to press effectively to make the action occur, so small T Rex fans might have a little more trouble activating things than one might like, but there's a next to it, which bigger guys will soon figure out.

I picked this up because I have a Jurassic world toys truck, which is supposed to hold the dinosaur in the back. There's like this included shell that comes up over the top and is supposed to have the dinosaur's head sticking up out of the shell, and I thought that this T Rex, being from the same line, would fit gracefully in the back of that truck. Nope, this thing is huge. Huge huge. Check the measurements before expecting this to dovetail with any other toys because T Rex is a big dude.

The size and the snapping jaws action really contributes to the awesome gift presentation this makes. Does it have a lot of long-term play potential? I'm not really sure that it does, frankly. I think in our house, once I get tired of tripping over it, I'm going to relegate it to being a backyard toy and just allow it to slowly stop working. However, right now the kids are having a blast creating scenes for T Rex to come in and stomp. He is particularly good it crashing through block towers.

text_fidelity_a:
Journey Girls 18" Doll, Callie The Journey Girls dolls are 18" dolls. Clothing-wise, they appear to be compatible with other 18" dolls such as American Girl, Playtime by Eimmie, the Our Generation dolls, or even the 18" Adora dolls. At this price point, they are definitely an affordable play option for younger girls. Like the Adora dolls, they have plastic shoulder and upper torso area and the lower torso is cloth. (The AG, Playtime by Eimmie, and Our Generation dolls all have completely cloth torsos). The Journey Girls dolls do not turn their head well, but their face sculpts are all unique to each doll (again, similar to the Adora dolls, as the Playtime by Eimmie seem to all have the same face sculpt with different skin shades and paint jobs). I personally find the Adora dolls to be my favorite 18" alternative to the American Girl dolls, but they are still at a high enough price point that I would not want to hand one over to my 5 year old for unsupervised play. The Playtime by Eimmie dolls have a full cloth body, making them softer and more huggable than the Journey Girls dolls (and probably more appealing for younger girls), and they are about the same price point. The style of clothing the Journey Girls have, as well as their sculpted plastic upper torsos, they give the impression of teenagers rather than younger girls, which makes them very appealing to the 8-10 year old set.

The packaging indicated Callie is from Japan, and she definitely has more almond-shaped eyes than Meredith. Her light skin, brown hair (instead of black), and eye shape reminded my bi-racial girls of themselves. That is the true gift of doll lines that have unique face sculpts, to provide a mirror so all little girls can have a doll that resembles them, as well as a truly diverse line of dolls.
text_fidelity_b: Journey Girls 18" Doll, Callie

Crayola Modeling Dough Pony Play Land - 33 pieces This is a cute modeling dough kit, and many toddlers and preschoolers will enjoy playing with it. But there are some issues for thrifty parents and grandparents to consider to determine if you are getting good value for your money:

What you are basically getting with this set that is hard to replicate at an arts and crafts store are the pony molds. The clay itself you can get by buying Play Doh, or making your own clay at home (typical recipes are very easy to find on the Internet). If you are at all artistic yourself, you could make your own molds of plaster. Though, granted, plastic molds like the ones in this kit are not breakable like plaster molds can be. Another question to ask yourself might be: Why bother with molds at all? Why not let small children model clay (which you can make yourself very cheaply) in any form they choose? This is much more creative than using someone else's molds and often much more fun.

Note that there are small pieces in this set that are a potential swallowing hazard, so it is not recommended for children under the age of 3, and even then, it is important to supervise small children when playing with this set.
text_fidelity_b: Crayola Modeling Dough Pony Play Land - 33 pieces

Mattel Disney Princess Royal Castle Disney Princess Royal Castle is a cute castle that is sure to be a hit with young princesses everywhere who are addicted to the Disney Princesses and love anything associated with them. This castle is much like other Disney castles available on the market, with a few added accessories and everything a young girl needs to enjoy hours of imaginative play.

I have two girls who have been Disney fanatics since a young age and still love anything related to Disney- especially the princesses. Their love of Belle, Snow White, Sleeping Beauty, Aerial, and the other princesses was reason enough to bring this toy into the house. Taking it from the box and assembling a few items was all it took to get the castle ready for play. In no time at all, they were running upstairs to find all of their Disney Princess dolls and bringing then downstairs to play with their new castle.

Disney Princess Royal Castle is a cute castle and very girly in appearance, making it just right for Disney Princess fans. My girls like the castle and they love anything that accommodates their Disney princess dolls. They also like making up stories as they play, but they and I both agree that this castle isn't they greatest one with which they have played. One reason is the lack of any sound effects, movements, etc. I am thankful that the castle includes no lights or anything that requires batteries, but it would be nice if it at least offered some mechanical movements, sound chips, or something else. Another issue is the small upper level. This is where the bedroom is located and it is much smaller than the area below. It would be better if the two levels were a little more even.

My girls love anything Disney Princess related and they like this castle, but they do not rank it among their favorites and it is easy to see why. The lack of at least a simple sound effect, the small number of accessories, and the lack of folding or another way to make storing easier all add up to an average toy overall.
text_fidelity_b: Mattel Disney Princess Royal Castle

LEGO Disney Frozen Elsa's Magical Ice Palace 43172 Toy Castle Building Kit with Mini Dolls, Castle Playset with Popular Frozen Characters Including Elsa, Olaf, Anna and More (701 Pieces) I’m a lover of the really big LEGO sets, especially the Creator buildings (e.g., Cinderella’s Castle; the Detective’s Office) and the Technic heavy construction equipment models (e.g., the Bucket Wheel Excavator). In my opinion, this medium-sized set, the DISNEY FROZEN ELSA’S MAGICAL ICE PALACE (41148) is one of LEGO’s very best efforts.

The set has lots of beautiful transparent blue bricks, and a couple of specialized large panels for the castle that are transparent blue with embedded silver sparkles. The transparent blue bricks exactly match Elsa’s blue from the “Frozen” movie.

If you’ve seen the movie, you will love the spiral staircase that expands and rises up with a twist of the ball at the top--very much like the icy castle walls that rose up magically in response to Elsa’s sweeping movements in the movie. As is always true with LEGO sets, it's fun to see, as you build, how the simple bricks become furniture, chandeliers, doorways, and other details.

The set has minifigures of Olaf, Elsa, Anna, a snow monster, and small snowmen. The balconied castle is furnished with a chandelier, a bed with coverlet, a table and chairs, a music stand, and a kitchen. Stickers printed on sparkly silver paper go onto the moving castle doors to complete the dazzling look of the ice palace. And despite all the detail, this set is fairly easy to build.

LEGO Juniors Cruz Ramirez Race Simulator 10731 Building Kit If you are not familiar with the Lego Junior sets, here is the run down. The Legos are same size as the regular Legos. So tiny pieces for you to step on and feel a pain beyond your wildest imagination is highly probable. These are not a size of Lego that is between Duplo and Lego, which is what I initially thought they would be. It's what I hoped they would be. Instead, Lego Juniors are the first step to learning how to build sets with Legos using instructions. There are fewer pieces and the builds are more simplified for a younger child.

The instructions are similar to Ikea instructions, no words, but pictures that show you each step towards your newly assembled Danish minimalist furniture. The instructions are actually easy to follow and my five year old can mostly figure it out. However, I would not recommend this for any child under the age of 5, and I would highly advise to supervise while building. When I mean supervise, I don't mean just be in the room. I mean actually be there next to your child. Why? Because at 4-6 years of age, kids want to play with the Legos. It's not about building and then displaying them, they want to actually roll the cars around and move the people and have the cars crash into each other and the people jump off of buildings. Why is this a problem? It's not a problem until the pieces go missing and then you cannot build the set anymore. Lego Juniors does not realistically take into consideration that its intended age target plays rough and they are not going to be mindful to keep track of all the pieces. Thus, this exposes one of the issues with specific building sets. With free form building sets losing several pieces this is not much of an issue, but since every piece must be placed in a specific order, upon losing several, the set becomes unusable.

All that being said, if you kid loved Cars 3 and loves Legos, then this is the set for you. Just to give you an idea, this item retails for $9.99. Over the holidays, it was on sale here on Amazon and at places like Target, Walmart, and ToysRUs for $7.99. I've seen it retail for $12.99 at small business toy stores.

In addition, do not buy any Lego building set without a Lego tool. A lot of these sets have flat pieces that will get stuck and the Lego tool is your only key to sanity of getting those buggers apart! [[ASIN:B0076VIZBW LEGO Classic Brick Separator 630 Building Kit]]
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Juniors Cruz Ramirez Race Simulator 10731 Building Kit

Swimways Dry Float Lounger Pool Float, Translucent Inflatable Recliner Chair for Adults with Fast Inflation, Foot Rest & Cup Holder These products, both the dry float lounger and the socializer are prime examples of why I test products the way I do prior to writing my review.

When I initially received these products and inflated them I was fairly impressed with the design and comfort - by 18 days later both were flat lumps of rubber in the trash.

First the socializer never held air. After inflation by the following morning it had deflated to around 70% capacity. I put it under water in the pool and discovered multiple small defects in 2 seams.

The dry float lounger lasted a bit longer at 18 days but then was found flat due to a separation at the seam.

It is important to note neither of these were ever used by children or in any rough play as when I review products I adhere to strict guidelines - and there are no children in the home.

While the socializer is listed as a dry float it appears the user’s calves and feet would be in the water. The lounger pool float is perfect for those who prefer to float completely out of the water. When floating on this no part of the body is submerged in the water.

While 88-90% of the world’s population is right handed this manufacturer chose to place the cup holder on the left side and made it too small to hold a standard 12 Oz can for both of these floats. This is simply poor designing.

While these floats come with a small patch kit, these are only helpful when repairing a puncture and absolutely will not hold a torn seam.

While these floats appeared to have promise initially, in well under a month they proved to be poorly designed, and of substandard construction and materials.

I would not recommend either of these products.
text_fidelity_b: Swimways Dry Float Lounger Pool Float, Translucent Inflatable Recliner Chair for Adults with Fast Inflation, Foot Rest & Cup Holder

text_fidelity_a:
K’NEX Revolution Ferris Wheel Building Set – 344 Pieces with Battery Powered Motor – Ages 7+ Engineering Education Toy [[VIDEOID:5795137e2a23bd3d76a56d2b9446c889]] If you’re already familiar with K’Nex building sets, this K’NEX THRILL RIDES-REVOLUTION FERRIS WHEEL is a simple, fast build. The Ferris wheel is big, but it doesn’t require a lot of pieces. Also, much of the assembly involves building duplicate parts that combine to make the wheel and its swinging gondolas.

The set is recommended for age 7+, and that sounds reasonable (assuming that an adult provides some initial help with making the connections, and assists with lifting the wheel onto the axle). Each shape of piece is a different color, which detracts from the appearance of the finished Ferris wheel, but makes the construction simpler. There aren’t many “snowflake” connections, which I usually have to puzzle over to get the right orientation. (K’Nex pieces are much harder to work with than LEGO pieces.) The instructions are reasonably clear. This set took me about 5 hours to build (from opening the box to completion, working at a leisurely pace).

Unfortunately, the finished “thrill ride” isn’t very thrilling. Like a full-sized amusement park ride, the Ferris wheel doesn’t do much—it just goes around and around in a circle. Also, it does NOT have a variable speed control—you cannot start, stop, or speed up the wheel gradually (like a real ride). Although the motor has a single speed, it does run in forward and reverse directions. The motor is powered by two AA batteries (not included).

For the Ferris wheel to turn properly, one edge of the inner wheel track must be settled into the groove on the “gear wheel” attached to the motor. You can easily fiddle with the base to adjust things so that the track and groove always make good contact. Because it’s sort of boring and lacks a variable speed control, I rate this K’Nex Ferris Wheel kit at 4 stars (“I like it” on the official Amazon scale).
text_fidelity_b: K’NEX Revolution Ferris Wheel Building Set – 344 Pieces with Battery Powered Motor – Ages 7+ Engineering Education Toy

When I received this item I was a bit surprised at how large it is, bigger than I expected. I was thinking this would be approximately the size of a bread loaf pan (a testament to how terrible my sense of measure is), so when the box arrived I was surprised when I opened it to find this large plastic truck.

This truck is all plastic which has some pluses and minuses about it. It’s not all that expensive, which would not be the case if it was metal or had metal parts in it. It’s completely waterproof, and it is made well enough to handle some limited abuse. It is not made of heavy-grade plastic, though, so if it is thrown or stood upon it could break.

There are moving parts but everything is manual. No levers, no buttons, no wheels other than the tires, so play isn’t as automated. This may or may not frustrate a young child, though that depends on the child and not the toy. It’s not a toy for the impatient.

This is a decent toy though there are some trade-offs. For the price it is a good unit that will keep a patient child busy. It is not the sturdiest nor is it the most technologically advanced, so it can be broken if handled very roughly and it may prove frustrating for a child who expects some automation.

text_fidelity_a:
Winning Moves Games Pretty Princess Board Game I am a board game afficionado. I own over 200 different strategy, social or silly games, and you'd better believe that my daughter is a gamer in waiting. Of course, as a young boy, Pretty Pretty Princess wasn't on my radar for myself, but I knew the name and the concept, and when it was my time to find a copy for my kid, there's no way I was paying the multiple hundreds for the original 80's item.

So I was thrilled when an appropriately priced remake made it's way to my house, and all it took was reading the name to hook my daughter (and interestingly, my wife as well) into a quest to become the most beautiful in all the realm.

The box for this one opens upside down for some reason, and one you get inside, you'll find a spinner, an odd, nearly blank game board, and some teeny tiny jewels to bling out your ensemble. Play is simple - you spin the spinner, attempt to move aroudn the circular board to earn all your gems, and the first one to get everything is crowned (literally) the prettiest princess.

Perhaps the most striking thing is the lack of effort they put into the board and spinner. Both are of reasonable thickness and sturdy, but there is almost nothing on the board in terms of graphic design outside of the logo on the field of white, and the spinner is literally numbers. They may have changed the font away from Times New Roman, but that's all there is to it. It looks like a high school kid's graphic design project, and not one that's going to earn high marks from the teacher.

That said, it's good to have this game back in print again, even if the game play is not particularly solid, and even if the graphics leave quite a bit to be desired. As I said, all I needed to do to get my little one to play was to tell her the name of the game, and my wife jumped right in on the nostalgia boat as well.
text_fidelity_b: Winning Moves Games Pretty Princess Board Game

ThinkFun Shadows in the Forest Play in the Dark Board Game for Kids and Families Age 8 and Up - Fun and Easy to Learn with Innovative and Unique Gameplay ThinkFun Shadows in the Forest Play in the Dark Board Game for Kids and Families Age 8 and Up - Fun and Easy to Learn with Innovative and Unique Gameplay is a game every age will enjoy! Kids as little as 3 love hiding and seeking and older adults love the memories of hiding and seeking out your playmates from their youth. The game can be played with 2 to 7 players.

This game is beautifully made with hard cardboard of a nice dark looking forest with a stone path. While putting the trees, stump and rock formations together, you will want to put the die under a light so it will glow in the dark for game play. You then place the masks on the Shadowling creatures. The Seeker gets to roll the die and move the lantern, after his eyes are closed, so the other player (s) can hide the little masked Shadowlings.

As the Seeker moves around the board, should any light hit any Shadowling- exposing them, their mask is removed and they are frozen and cannot move until another Shadowling can come and help him. Should all the Shadowlings end up together hiding in the same spot with their masks on, they win. Should the Seeker expose them all, freezing them, the Seeker wins. The room must be pitch black, so the tiny lantern can cast shadows and expose the hiding Shadowlings. A wonderful game of Hide & Seek played in pitch blackness that all ages will enjoy. 5 STARS.
text_fidelity_b: ThinkFun Shadows in the Forest Play in the Dark Board Game for Kids and Families Age 8 and Up - Fun and Easy to Learn with Innovative and Unique Gameplay

Craziest thing… almost a year later, when we went On vacation and met up for dinner at the house I sent this too..(can you follow that..?!) to my happy surprise- they were all playing awkward turtles!! Yep, the game I had sent to them almost a year prior!! (could have been contrived Sure-but, from the wear and tear on the game… I knew they had been using it all along.)

Of course, we went to have Dinner with the adults at the house.. But, their group of teen/20+ yr olds were laughing hysterically in the other room having “game night“ and I promise, they were having way more fun than we were!!

I peaked in on the gameplaying and the concept looked pretty straightforward. Basically, divided into two teams… One member has an awkward word and tries to describe it to their team- if guessed correctly they get points! And the game sort of back-and-forths from there… Funny, quirky, annoying, cringe worthy, racy words all make up the options.. These kids were playing the game when we arrived- 2hr. Later we left... And they were still playing! (No! Not the same round but, plenty of rounds and all entertained long enough to still be having fun hours later.)

To me, this is the best type of endorsement one can have… Seeing a game in action and hearing the laughter as it was being played. This told me all I needed to know… The game was a hit for the crowd at hand- it kept them happily playing for hours. Combined it with the ease of which it takes to “learn” the game.. And you’ve got a winner in my book!
text_fidelity_b: da Vinci's Room Awkward Turtle The Word Party Card Game with a Dirty Sense of Humor for Groups of 4 or More People

Hasbro Gaming Sorry Spin My family has really enjoyed playing this updated version of an old favorite. The basic rules are the same as in the original Sorry! Each player has four pawns to move around the board from Start to Home. You draw a card to find out how many spaces you can move your game piece. Landing on another player's pawn sends them back to start as does the Sorry! card, just as in the classic version.

What's different about Sorry Spin is the spinning board. The center circle is the main board, with connecting circles for each color's home which fit together like gears. The challenge of the spinning board is your home is contantly changing position in relation to the main board. You may be just a few spaces away from reaching your home track when the board will spin and you will end up all the way across the board from your home.

It took about 5 minutes to assemble the game board, which seems very sturdy. We had some trouble spinning the board on a slick surface (wood table, counter top), but when we placed it on a placemat, it worked fine. A nice addition is a box that can be assembled and used to store the cards.

This is a great family game which is faster paced than the original version of the game due to the spinning board and a shorter path between start and home. Also any number gets a pawn out of start. (unlike the original which requires a 1 or 2). Older kids and adults will enjoy the suggested variation of the two-player game in which each person selects two different colors instead of only one.
text_fidelity_b: Hasbro Gaming Sorry Spin

text_fidelity_a:
Franklin Sports Giant Wooden Dice These dice are beautifully made of solid pine. Playing games with these are fun but play responsibly. Displaying the dice as works of art is equally as great.

Provided in the package:
- Six die that weigh a combined 4.6 pounds. (See the attached pictures for an idea of size relative to two of my cats and their water fountain.)
- A strong canvas pouch for carrying the dice.
- A folded one-page pamphlet with two game variations and a sample score card for copying.

Each die is beautiful and each "number point" (i.e. dots) on the same die face is painted a rich coffee brown or dark tan. However, the "number points" are various shades of coffee brown on each side of the same die, so there is a slight inconsistency in color there. Nevertheless, this does not take away from their beauty. One should discount the "life-sized" claim. They are large but all of them stacked three high, side-by-side, do not even reach the height of a poised cat as you can see from my photos. When used for play instead of art, the round edge of each die provides for a smooth roll and reduction of injury to property or person. Although this is rated for ages 6 and above, I HIGHLY RECOMMEND children, adults, and pets stay far back when rolling the dice.

My boyfriend and I played the first game on my inside carpet since it was raining outside. I made sure to remove any items that could break around the area we were playing and I had to keep shooing the cats away. I originally thought we had to roll all six die at once (which is impossible). Therefore, when playing the two games in the instructions, roll each die one at a time because they are too large to roll together. The instructions should say that, however, because the first thought I had is "How am I going to roll these six die all at once," when the instructions said "roll the dice"?

My boyfriend loved the dice and the game even though I won. Since each die is heavy, it is extremely important to throw each die gently. I can see unsupervised children or drunk adults throwing these at each other and causing serious damage or death. As long as everyone plays responsibly, hours of fun and friendly competition are awaiting those who play this lawn or carpeted basement "game."
text_fidelity_b: Franklin Sports Giant Wooden Dice

text_fidelity_a:
Barbie Chicken Farmer Doll & Playset and Licensed Storytelling Pack w/ CDU - Jurassic (Sweater Dress) I just love the new generation of Barbies. While I personally didn't play with Barbies as a young one, the fact that they have more normal body shapes with Daisy and others, different ethnicities, the sports Barbies who are able to actually move well, and Ken and Barbie doing ordinary, more usual things that kids would be familiar with like the set that has Ken doing the laundry, and this set that has Barbie being a chicken farmer. I love it!

Though I think of Barbies as being for slightly older children than my three-year-old daughter, she absolutely loved this set and knew exactly how she wanted to play with it. Putting the chickens in the nest, collecting the eggs into the bucket, moving Barbie around and having conversations with the chickens, making the chickens say peep peep peep!

As for the set, my only suggestion would be to make the eggs able to come out of the a container. Even if this means that most of the eggs immediately got lost, it would provide so much more opportunity for fun and creativity. In order to allow my daughter to collect eggs into the bucket, I made a few eggs out of oven baked clay so that she would have a little bit more opportunity for interactive play.

My complaints about this Barbie doll are my usual complaints, I wish that this Barbie was shaped a little bit more like Daisy, and I wish that this Barbie moved a little bit more like the sports Barbies. I wish that all Barbies off the shelf would come with more functional joints so that Barbie could do more interesting things. However! My three-year-old has noticed no lack, and I think the fact that Barbie is rather inflexible makes her somewhat easier to get dressed, which is fun. This Barbie has a very sweet, engaging face, and even though this toys for children, I'll be honest and say that I genuinely enjoy playing with this set with my daughter.
text_fidelity_b: Barbie Chicken Farmer Doll & Playset and Licensed Storytelling Pack w/ CDU - Jurassic (Sweater Dress)

text_fidelity_a: Warashibe Wooden Secret Puzzle Box, 5 Sun 21 Steps, Japan Made, with Original Gift Box I have some from the 1940s that my father brought home from World War II.  One is more traditional - it is made of wood and looks like a stack of faux books with a larger book on its side both on the bottom and top.  The "page" piece of the bottom book slides open to an area that holds the key, the bottom book slides back, the center book's spine slides down to reveal the keyhole.  Insert the key, turn it and the book on top opens to a velvet lined interior.  The top book has several veneers to create a border and little birds flying across the top.  My other puzzle box has a large veneered diamond on top of the heavily veneered box.  Slide the diamond back and the box can be opened.  Center the diamond on the closed box and it "locks" it.  This box is more complicated that either of my other puzzle boxes mentioned here, but one thing they all share in common is the veneer work.  This box features very geometric veneering and it is quite pretty.  The complexity of the puzzle to open the box is a lot more fun and interesting for this box - it's really neat!  Yes, they are expensive, but for a reason - the veneer work and all the moving parts of this box requires a seriously high amount of quality control.  Worth it, for sure!
text_fidelity_b: Warashibe Wooden Secret Puzzle Box, 5 Sun 21 Steps, Japan Made, with Original Gift Box

text_fidelity_a:
Adora My Cuddle & Coo Baby “Cuppy Cake” - Touch Activated Doll with 5 Sounds: She Cries, Coos, Giggles, Kisses Back & Says Momma Just like I had thought before actually receiving this, you are probably thinking that this is a hefty pricetag for a doll that doesn't even have the American Girl logo attached to it... well, move over Pleasant Company (yeah, I said it), because Adora is a new generation of dolls that are not only kid approved (my girls, ages ranging from 6-10, all love their Adora dolls) but it is also parent/caregiver/teacher approved (I would know, as I'm technically all 3, haha). My girls love this doll because she's so cuddly and lifelike, and I love her because I have spent some time actually researching the Adora company... and let me just say THANK YOU for finally coming out with a line of dolls that are crafted from SAFE and nontoxic materials! No more feeling that tiny pang of worry ("mom guilt" lol) whenever my daughter is snuggled up with her doll. I love the peace of mind that comes from knowing the dolls arms, legs, and face are made of vinyl and are BPA free. Finally, a toy company with ethics!

Many of Adoras dolls are machine washable (this particular one has electronics and therefore is not, so care must be taken when wiping the vinyl parts and perhaps spraying a safe vinegar solution on the dolls plush core to keep clean and fresh). Honestly, I can't really comment on the electronic aspect of this doll, as I turned off that feature pretty early (i think it encourages better open-ended imaginative play that way... not to mention less annoying for cranky mommies lol). So you'll have to check other reviews for better details on that function.

All in all, yes, this is not a cheap doll. But in my humble opinion, you are getting a lot of value for your money with this doll. The brand has less expensive plush options too that are just as adorable, less expensive, and even machine washable (we have one and I'll be doing a review soon). The Adora line has a wide selection of dolls and accessories too by the way. I'm actually excited to buy some accessories because I feel like they are very competitively priced and plus it feels good to support such an ethical company that brings so much joy to children.

Grandparents, this is a gift that will not only make you the favorite grandparent, but will also please even the pickiest of health-conscious daughter-in-laws lol.

Two thumbs up for Adora!!

text_fidelity_a:
Schleich Portable Barn with Accessories The Schleich barn is made of wood and is of extremely high quality except for a problem with the clips and pieces of wood that hold the barn roof together.

The barn opens into two separate unattached halves that slide together at right angles like a puzzle. There are latches on either short side of the barn that can be unlatched to display each half. The barn can be left open or closed. When closed it is easy to carry. A cow, chicken, donkey, lamb, hay bale, basket, red and green vegetables, and a pitch fork and broom are the accessories included. The barn doors on the long side of the barn open in both front and back. The color is vibrant and the farm animals are very realistic.

The only negative I found is that the entire barn is held together with clips that come apart. The clips are not its strongest point. The four clips on either side of the barn roof on mine would not hold up the roof and the boards keep falling off. I tried for over 30 minutes to get two of the clips seated correctly but neither side would snap in place. My boyfriend also looked at this barn and he could not get the clips to seat firmly in place either. He did say, however, that this is a well-made toy. According to the side of the box below the Germany label, it says this is made in Slovakia.

The clips and vegetable pieces that come with the barn can present a choking hazard to a small child. If the child is of that age where items are frequently "tasted," then I recommend adult supervision while the child is playing with this barn. The box indicates that this is not for children under 3 years of age and does state that the small parts present a choking hazard. This is typical of many toys with small parts, however.

Other than this, I got this for my friend's son to play with and he's going to love it. However, he'll have to play with the two roof slats off since they will fall off in its current condition. If the unit I received did not have this problem, I would have rated this 5 stars. Since mine does have this problem, I'm rating it 3. Had I purchased this unit and not received it for review, I would have returned it for a replacement. Since the three other reviewers have not complained about this issue, I suspect it is either a new issue introduced in recent manufacturing design or the unit I received is slightly defective. If there are no other recent reviews that complain about the clips and barn roof, then I would consider this a 5-star toy where I was the one exception. Nevertheless, this defect will not detract from my friend's son enjoyment as young children rarely notice those things.
text_fidelity_b: Schleich Portable Barn with Accessories

text_fidelity_a: Brainwaves: The Astute Goose - A Kosmos Game from Thames & Kosmos | Fun, Scientist Approved, Family-Friendly Games to Sharpen Your Mind & Train Your Brain, for Ages 8+ This card game can be played solo or with up to five players. It is intended for ages eight and up. The large cards are easy to hold and the things you're supposed to memorize on each card are clear to see. There are 25 suspect cards which include variations in color, clothing, and animals. You place three to six of these cards out (depending on the difficulty level you desire) and memorize each card before turning them upside down. There are six number cards that you place above each suspect so that you know which suspect to talk about when you roll the dice. The dice roll tells you which suspect to talk about and which feature (color, clothing, or animal) that you need to remember correctly for that suspect. If the player is able to correctly remember that feature, they keep the card and score a point, but if they remember wrong, the rest of the players each have a chance to guess until someone gets it right or no one does. That suspect card is replaced with a new one, and everyone has a chance to look at the new card. Thus, you are constantly having to remember new information for each position. This can be a fun way to train your brain to remember better, but some people might find it too frustrating.
text_fidelity_b: Brainwaves: The Astute Goose - A Kosmos Game from Thames & Kosmos | Fun, Scientist Approved, Family-Friendly Games to Sharpen Your Mind & Train Your Brain, for Ages 8+

text_fidelity_a:
Crayola Glow Book Seeing commercials for the Glow Book, I've been interested in this toy for my 9 year old. Obviously commercials are made to show the absolute best of a product, so I expected it to be much less than what was advertised. I have to admit it's almost as cool as the advertisements. However, the best way to discover if a toy is really worth it is to test it out on more than just a few kids. I went with those who were interested in art. Thus, this is judging based on kids who are already fans of art.

Honest opinions from kids:

1. It came with pages you could trace for kids who can't draw too well.
2. If you make a mistake, it's easy to erase it, but it's hard to make it all clean. You really have to rub well to erase mistakes or it leaves smearing behind. They should have something to erase it better. At least you can use it more than one time.
3. It needs more pages. You have plastic pages you draw on and the lights come on to show each page. It makes everything look like it's moving when the lights flash. The pages also aren't very straight.
4. I really like to play with the glow book because it is fun. You just have to get used to using it.
5. It was just like a movie. I could color and draw it just how I pleased.
6. It would be nice if there could be just a little more colors because it shows purple in some of the tracings, but there is no purple. Maybe some black to show outlines, too. It just comes with six colors: tan, pink, yellow, blue, red and green.

From an adult's perspective - it definitely has keep the interest going with the kids. It's not a toy that ends up on the shelf - lost and forgotten. However, the price tag is a bit high for something that's so simple. I have seen Amazon have excellent deals on the Glow Book, however, and think if you are patient and give yourself time to find a great deal, you will. Anything less than $20 would be great. I agree with one of the children that it could use more colors. Especially when dealing with kids interested in art. For younger kids, the small amount of color choices is probably fine. Glass cleaner takes care of the smudges you'll find after repeated use by kids. After a few mistakes, the drawing takes on a foggy/dusty look - thus making it harder to see the pictures "move" clearly. Downside is it can't be cleaned until the child is entirely finished. Definitely stick with the manufacturer age recommendation of 6 years and up. This toy is not made well enough to handle rough use from younger kids.
text_fidelity_b: Crayola Glow Book
